content:
incident-bot: PAGER: hosted-runtime/kvcache: rapid spike in KV cache memory + OOMs across 3 clusters. error-rate: 18% -> 62% in 5m. links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/kvcache?from=now-10m

incident-bot: Top error signature: "kvcache: allocation failed: context-window: 512k tokens" (samples attached)

sara: ack. I'm oncall. investigating now. which customers showing errors?

mike: saw alerts from eu1-hosted and us-west. A few large customers (id: cust-182, cust-97) report hallucinations + timeouts. CS is waiting.

sara: copying runtime eng. @cheng can you join?

cheng: here. seeing large prefetched context sizes from some requests -> kvcache growth. could be long prompts + continuous batching merging sessions.

vika: I'm pulling traces for the highest-error nodes. suspect prefetch concurrency spiking after the new batching change rolled last night.

sara: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce continuous-batching window to 100ms 2) throttle prefetch concurrency to 2 3) aggressive eviction policy (TTL+min-entries) 4) temp route affected traffic to smaller model variant. execute in that order?

cheng: +1. Doable without full restart for 1+2 via config hotpatch. eviction needs rolling restart on kvcache pods. routing change is control-plane only.

dev-runtime: I'll apply hotpatch for batching/prefetch first. applying now to eu1-hosted.

dev-runtime: PATCH: /services/kvcache/config

```
continuous_batching.window_ms: 100
prefetch.max_concurrency: 2
```

rolling apply -> started (5 pods target)

sara: monitoring memory and error-rate.

vika: memory on the first pod dropped from 86% -> 52% after hotpatch. errors down to 30% in that shard. good signal.

mike: CS update queued to customers: "We identified a memory amplification triggered by very long prompts. We have applied emergency throttles and routing changes to reduce impact. We'll follow up once stable."

sara: next: eviction policy. I want an aggressive evict threshold: keep-last-n = 4 and TTL=30m for hotfix. That needs pods restart. Is that safe?

cheng: safe. do a staggered restart for the kvcache podset with a 60s gap to avoid capacity dip. I'll own the rollout.

dev-runtime: initiating restart sequence on us-west cluster. Pod kvcache-7 terminated -> started. memory on new pod low, but next pod shows the spike, restarting now.

incident-bot: NOTE: routed traffic % to fallback model increased to 18% after routing change. No 5xx on fallback paths.

vika: after 3/5 restarts in us-west, overall cluster mem usage down 48%. Error-rate across clusters decreased to 12%.

sara: good. I'll keep pager open for 30m. @mike please flag any escalations from customers.

mike: will do. CS pinged cust-182 with immediate mitigation note. They asked for ETA on full fix. I'll tell them 2 hours + RCA later.

cheng: root cause hypothesis: continuous batching merged extremely long prompt prefixes (generated by a customer integration) into KV cache entries without upper bound => exponential kvmap growth when multiple sessions share similar prefixes. Regression window: batching change 13h ago.

sara: we should also add a hard max-kv-entry-size guard in runtime to avoid allocation blowups. can we ship a small patch?

cheng: I can prepare a minimal guard: if entry_size > 1MB then drop prefetch + log. Will PR and ship to staging in 30m.

dev-runtime: PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kvcache/pulls/482

```
if (entry.byte_size > 1_048_576) {
  skip_prefetch = true
  metric("kvcache.entry_skipped_large")
}
```

cheng: planning canary rollout after staging pass. will coordinate with oncall-2 for post-handoff verification.

oncall-2: I will take the 2nd half of the pager window (handoff at +45m). please leave notes in thread.

vika: adding quick telemetry to detect prefix amplification: emit histogram of per-request kventries_count and kv_total_bytes. alert if slope > 3x baseline. patching metrics now.

incident-bot: ALERT SUPPRESSED: error-rate threshold cleared in eu1 (now 8%). continuing observation.

mike: one customer (cust-97) still showing intermittent timeouts; we've routed their heavy sessions to dedicated capacity as a stopgap. They confirmed reduced failures.

sara: excellent. next actions list (I'm writing down):
- Cheng to ship guard PR and canary (in 2-3h)
- Dev-runtime to rollback batching change on next prod deploy if canary fails
- Vika to finalize amplification telemetry + alert
- Mike to coordinate customer comms and postmortem timeline
- Sara to draft incident summary for execs after stabilization

cheng: noted. will attach logs and the offending request samples to the PR.

dev-runtime: can we capture a sample of the offending prompt safely? make sure PII redact. I'll add a hook to mask tokens > 1024 characters.

vika: redaction done in staging capture. no PII stored.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: oncall -> oncall-2 at 2755557029.

sara: handing off. oncall-2 will verify canary and metrics for next 2 hours. I'll stay available for questions.

oncall-2: taking over. thanks all. will update thread if I see regressions. :thumbsup:

mike: sending CS follow-up: "We have applied mitigations, reduced error-rate significantly, and are deploying a guard to prevent recurrence. ETA on full fix: 3-4 hours with RCA to follow."

sara: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. creating postmortem ticket: INC-2755556789. thanks team — good coordination.
